item.text: The migration currently selects the latest history row, which can apply a later fee to an earlier approval, and it does not diagnose invalid imported fees. I’m changing the backfill to use the fee effective on `approved_at`, retaining legacy terms for old clients, and ensuring a new version omits both the old fee and prior decision.

item.text:
Implemented the migration and version creation changes.

- [migration.sql](/private/var/folders/vv/rc3f4h3505jfy6qnq3w7m93w0000gn/T/harness-eval-Lb3K6k/workspace/migration.sql) snapshots the fee effective on each subscription’s approval date. It reports invalid subscriptions and raises SQLSTATE `P0001` for missing or negative fees; the transaction leaves legacy data intact on failure.
- [schema.sql](/private/var/folders/vv/rc3f4h3505jfy6qnq3w7m93w0000gn/T/harness-eval-Lb3K6k/workspace/schema.sql) now represents the pre-migration schema.
- [subscriptions.ts](/private/var/folders/vv/rc3f4h3505jfy6qnq3w7m93w0000gn/T/harness-eval-Lb3K6k/workspace/subscriptions.ts) keeps legacy fee reads and inputs working. New versions omit the previous fee and pricing decision so a new fee can be decided.

Checks passed: `bun test` and a PostgreSQL 18 migration run with a subscription created before migration. The check confirmed the legacy fee remained readable and the approval-date fee was selected despite a later history entry.
